chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Kūfī, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Yazīd, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Ziyād, from Jaʿfar, from his father عليهما السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: “Whoever recites a verse of poetry from obscene speech, no salat (prayer) will be accepted from him on that day; and whoever recites it at night, no salat (prayer) will be accepted from him that night.”

key_terms.بَيْتِ شِعْرٍ: A line or verse of poetry
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, the speaker being quoted in the hadith
key_terms.صَلَاةٌ: Salat (prayer), the ritual worship whose acceptance is mentioned

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about reciting obscene poetry and the acceptance of salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith warns against reciting obscene or indecent poetry and links such speech to the non-acceptance of one’s salat (prayer) for that period. It underscores the ethical and spiritual effect of a person’s speech upon worship and devotional standing.
